SUBJECTIVE:
Patient is a 70 year old male who presents for general medical evaluation. He has recently moved to the Madison area and wishes to establish care.
 
HPI:
The patient's primary complaint is persistent fatigue. Patient noted onset of symptoms several months ago and feels it has been gradually worsening since that time. On questioning, he also relates feeling cold much of the time where other people are comfortable. He denies constipation, skin or hair changes. Weight has been stable. Appetite normal. There is no family history of thyroid disease.
 
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Hypertension - diagnosed at age 54. Initially treated with sodium restriction, diet, and exercise. Diuretics were started in approximately 1988 and have been taken sporadically since that time. Currently on Dyazide b.i.d.. Patient admits to poor compliance with medication regimen. No history to suggest end organ damage or coronary artery disease. Cardiovascular risk factors include a 20-pack-year history of smoking.
 
GERD - diagnosed by EGD approximately seven years ago. Symptoms well controlled with intermittent use of H2 blockers.
 
Cluster headaches - diagnosed in 1988 at age 54. Suffered from periodic clusters, occurring two to three times per year for the next five years. He has noted no recurrence of symptoms since 1993.
